correctness.rationale: The exact source Algorithm 3 maps to Euclidean projection of the residual onto a Gaussian vector in the complement of a trailing orthogonal direction window. Orthogonality of the current error to that window is inductive. Conditional rotational invariance yields a beta residual ratio depending only on deterministic complement dimension, hence mutual independence. A beta moment identity proves all finite moments and their sharp negative integrability boundary; the strong law proves the digamma exponent; the one-dimensional complement gives deterministic termination. Standalone numeric tests include nonnormalized source-algorithm equivalence and thousands of distribution-moment checks; these are supplementary, not proof.

value.rationale: The source papers supply expected-rate inequalities but not the exact distributional time course of a natural finite-memory solver. The moving-window independence theorem makes exact transient and stationary error laws available, showing when extra memory improves convergence, the distinction between mean and typical rates, and exactly which inverse-error moments exist. These are motivated solver-reliability questions rather than isolated arbitrary constants, and they are not implied by a finite-termination remark.
